_comment: 🔮️ Test-only references of the pets product (Protocol v2). Every case under ../🧪️tests names one of these oracles or the recorded no-oracle decision; the TypeScript twin (@semio-tech/pets) and the Rust twin (semio-framework-pets) are the subjects and are additionally held to each other. The Python references live inside the case adapters (🧪️tests/*/🐍️.py) and use numpy, scipy and jsonschema only. Shared vectors under ../🧫️fixtures are generated from those same adapters by the ticket scripts named in every feature, so a committed vector and its oracle can never disagree.

engine.implementation: numpy.sin and numpy.cos, numpy.random.SeedSequence.generate_state, numpy.linalg (inv, norm, matrix_power), numpy.interp, numpy.cumsum and numpy.searchsorted

oracles.rationale: The pets core is a deterministic fold restricted to exact arithmetic, square roots and 32-bit integer operations (design §2.4), so each of its numeric modules has a closed mathematical reading numpy evaluates independently: sine and cosine of 2π·t for the polynomial `sinTurns`/`cosTurns` (case 📐️turn-trigonometry, tolerance 1e-9 around an owned error bound of 1e-12); `numpy.random.SeedSequence(key).generate_state(count)` for the counter-based draws, whose words must match bit for bit (case 🎲️counter-randomness); 3×3 homogeneous matrix products and `numpy.linalg.inv` for the forward kinematics and inverses of the rig (case 🦴️rig-solving); `numpy.linalg.norm` for the look offset and `numpy.linalg.matrix_power` of the semi-implicit Euler step matrix for the gaze and settling springs (cases 👀️gaze-tracking, 🪀️spring-settling); membership on a sampled grid and closed forms for perches and strides (case 🏞️terrain-walking); `numpy.cumsum` with `numpy.searchsorted` for weighted picks and the drift arithmetic of rapport (cases 🧠️behavior-choice, 🤝️bond-dynamics). Surveyed and declined: gl-matrix, d3-ease and polygon-clipping are JavaScript libraries and can judge the TypeScript twin inside its unit suites only, never the Rust twin; pure-rand and seedrandom implement other generator families than the SeedSequence hash-mix; mathjs has no SeedSequence and no bit-exact 32-bit stream.

packages.role: Array arithmetic, `numpy.interp` between keys and the sampled grids the scipy routines are evaluated on.

oracles.rationale: Three parts of the core solve something a general numeric library solves differently: the cubic Bézier easing inverts x(s) by 48 bisection steps, which `scipy.optimize.brentq` on the same polynomial reproduces within 1e-9 (case 🎞️animation-sampling, with `numpy.interp` for the linear stretches between keys); the hop between perches is a ballistic arc integrated tick by tick, which `scipy.integrate.solve_ivp` and the roots of the arc bound (case 🦘️hop-ballistics); and every activity must stay reachable from every other through the weights of the behaviour table, which `scipy.sparse.csgraph` decides on the transition graph (case 🧠️behavior-choice). Surveyed and declined: d3-ease has no general cubic-bezier (its eases are fixed families; it judges the TypeScript twin's `smoothstep` only), bezier-easing is not in the lockfile, and CSS engines cannot be reached from the harness.

The contract 🧬️schema/🔣️.json is JSON Schema draft-07 and normative; the product validates menageries, species and ensembles with its own validator (menagerieIssues, speciesIssues, ensembleIssues) and links no schema library at runtime. python-jsonschema's Draft7Validator reads the normative file itself and judges every committed document of case 🧬️schema-conformance: the sample menagerie, each of its species and its ensemble must conform; every structurally broken document must break the schema at the keyword and pointer its vector names; and every document that breaks a rule of design §3 is judged for what the schema can say about it — it either conforms (the rule lies beyond JSON Schema: duplicate ids, unresolved references, bone order, key order, loop seams, gait clips, hover, duplicate bonds and scenes) or breaks the named keyword (ranges, colours, ease abscissas, the two different species of a bond, the core of a cast). The codes and pointers of those rule findings are recomputed beside it in the adapter by a second implementation written from the design text — a supplement that holds the two cores to one reading of the rules, not third-party evidence. ajv (pets-ajv-structure) judges the same contract inside the TypeScript unit suite — two independent schema engines.

Judges the owned validator inside the unit suite `🔨️modules/✅️validation/🧪️tests/🔬️unit` of @semio-tech/pets (vitest, devDependency of the core package): ajv compiles the normative 🧬️schema/🔣️.json and, for every tested menagerie, species and ensemble, accepts the document exactly when the owned validator reports no finding the schema can express, and rejects every structurally broken document at the pointer the owned validator names. It is the JavaScript engine beside python-jsonschema (pets-jsonschema), which judges the same contract in the Protocol v2 case.

engine.implementation: mat2d (multiply, invert, translate, rotate, scale, fromRotation) and vec2.transformMat2d

oracles.rationale: Judges the owned affine arithmetic and the owned sine and cosine inside the unit suites `🔨️modules/🦴️rig/🧪️tests/🔬️unit` and `🔨️modules/📐️trigonometry/🧪️tests/🔬️unit` of @semio-tech/pets (vitest, devDependency of the core package). gl-matrix's mat2d has the layout of the rig's `Affine`: `compose` must equal `mat2d.multiply(parent, local)` and `transform` must equal `vec2.transformMat2d` bit for bit, `invert` must agree with `mat2d.invert` within 1e-11 and answer the identity exactly where gl-matrix refuses to invert, and every solved skeleton must agree with the chain gl-matrix translates, rotates, scales and multiplies bone by bone. `sinTurns` and `cosTurns` are held to `mat2d.fromRotation` on 65 537 angles over ±8 turns within the module's error bound of 1e-12. It is the JavaScript engine beside numpy (pets-numpy), which judges the same modules in the Protocol v2 cases 🦴️rig-solving and 📐️turn-trigonometry; the React target registers the same library for its drawing rules (pets-react-gl-matrix).

engine.implementation: d3-ease easeLinear, easeQuadIn, easeQuadOut, easeCubicIn, easeCubicOut and easeCubicInOut

oracles.rationale: Judges the owned easing inside the unit suite `🔨️modules/🎞️animation/🧪️tests/🔬️unit` of @semio-tech/pets (vitest, devDependency of the core package). A polynomial ease is a cubic Bézier whose abscissa is linear (control points at one and two thirds), so `easeBezier` with those control points must reproduce d3-ease's `easeLinear`, `easeQuadIn`, `easeQuadOut`, `easeCubicIn` and `easeCubicOut` within 1e-13 on 1025 amounts; the CSS ease-in-out, which no d3 ease equals, is held to the family of `easeCubicInOut` (symmetric, rising, on the same side of the diagonal, never 0.1 apart). d3-ease has no general cubic-bezier: the bisection itself is judged by `scipy.optimize.brentq` (pets-scipy) in the Protocol v2 case 🎞️animation-sampling.

Judges the owned interval arithmetic of the perches inside the unit suite `🔨️modules/🏞️terrain/🧪️tests/🔬️unit` of @semio-tech/pets (vitest, devDependency of the core package). `perchesOf` cuts the free stretches of a surface with plain comparisons; polygon-clipping reaches the same stretches as geometry: the strip of the surface intersected with the viewport, minus the column of every keep-out whose box overlaps the headroom band above the strip with an area. On 300 generated layouts of surfaces and keep-outs the two must name the same perches. It is the JavaScript engine beside numpy (pets-numpy), which judges the perches by membership on a sampled grid in the Protocol v2 case 🏞️terrain-walking.

engine.implementation: mat2d (translate, rotate, scale, multiply, fromValues) and vec2.transformMat2d

oracles.rationale: Judges the owned SVG depiction of @semio-tech/pets-react inside its suite `🧪️tests/🖌️pet-depiction` (vitest in jsdom, devDependency of the react package). gl-matrix's mat2d has the layout of an SVG `matrix(a b c d e f)`; it composes the rig of the tested species bone by bone (translate, rotate, scale, then the parent's matrix), and every `transform` the depiction writes must parse back to those six numbers within the three decimals the drawing rules round to (design §6.2). It also carries points through what was written: the tip of a limb through the matrix of its group, and a pupil through bone, eye offset and lid squash, which must land where gl-matrix puts them. The frames the depiction is given are gl-matrix's own, so the suite does not lean on the core's rig solver, which numpy judges in case 🦴️rig-solving.

engine.implementation: aria-query `roles` map: the WAI-ARIA 1.2 role model with each role's superclasses, queried directly and through @testing-library/dom's `getRoles`, `queryAllByRole` and `isInaccessible`

oracles.rationale: Judges two claims of @semio-tech/pets-react inside its suites (vitest in jsdom, devDependency of the react package). In `🧪️tests/🫥️decorative-layer` the pet layer must be decoration (design §6.5): with a cast on stage, @testing-library/dom's accessibility tree — built on aria-query's role model — must hold no node of the layer (`getRoles` is empty for it, `isInaccessible` is true for the layer and every descendant) and a query for each of aria-query's concrete roles must find nothing in it. In `🧪️tests/📡️surface-survey` the default keep-outs must cover what a person can operate (design §6.3): every role the selector of controls names must be a concrete widget role by aria-query's superclass chains, and over a sample of native and ARIA elements the selector must match exactly those whose role — implicit by @testing-library/dom, or explicit — aria-query calls a widget. The geometry of the survey is held to shared vectors (`🧫️fixtures/📡️surface-survey`) computed by a second reading of the design written in Python from the design text (`generate_survey_vectors.py` of ticket 2026/10/02/QUIZ-PETS: tag and attribute tables instead of a selector engine, interval arithmetic) — a supplement, never third-party evidence; no library measures a page into surfaces and keep-outs by these rules. Frame pacing (`🧪️tests/⏲️frame-pacing`) runs on a hand-driven clock and on the fake clock of vitest itself.

noOracleDecisions.rationale: The stage (design §5) is this product's own simulation: events folded into actors that idle, walk, hop, fall, glance, blink and meet each other on surveyed perches. No third-party library simulates this model, and a second engine written to be compared with it would be this model again. Case 🎪️stage-trace therefore rests on scripted event logs committed as specification vectors — the projection is a digest of every frame's numbers — and on laws that hold for every log: actors stand on perches, never inside keep-outs, at most the mode's number of movers, at most one encounter, the same seed and events yield the same frames. Every building block the stage calls (trigonometry, randomness, rig, animation, terrain, behaviour) has a third-party oracle of its own. The TypeScript core and its Rust twin each replay every log, and the harness compares their projections digest for digest at every checkpoint: two separately compiled cores that agree on the IEEE-754 bit patterns of every frame are the `independent-implementations` substitute.

comparisonProfiles.description: Structural identity with the pets numeric parity tolerance of 1e-9 (design §10), applied as an absolute difference; projections compared under it are scaled so that 1e-9 is also their relative bound. Ids, kinds, orders, integers and every non-numeric field still compare exactly.

subjectFeatures.rationale: 🧪️ The pets crate re-exports its JSON codec (serde_json with `float_roundtrip`, so every committed decimal becomes the double JSON.parse and Python read) only under `sut`: the Rust subject adapters decode the shared vectors into the typed twins and encode their answers with it, while production builds of the crate stay free of serde_json.

oracleHostPackages.rationale: 📐️ Sine and cosine, SeedSequence words, homogeneous matrices, norms, matrix powers and cumulative weights of the numeric references.
🎞️ Root finding on the Bézier easing, integration of the hop arc and reachability of the behaviour graph.
🧬️ Draft 7 validation of every pets document against the normative schema.
